utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Good afternoon to everybody in the courtroom and to those listening and watching our procedures. I got the information, Mr. McCloskey, that there is an update about certain documents.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President, good afternoon. Good afternoon, Your Honours. I have some translation announcements. P01544C is done in English. P01990 is done in English. P02177 is a replacement of a partial translation that's now complete. P02211 is English and P02217 is done. And I'm told P02217 was that document you were concerned with yesterday, the one with the date stamp so that's now complete. And then P2168 is a replacement of the first page because that page was not legible so we now have a legible page.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Thank you very much. These documents will be now exhibits. The Registry will follow up on that. If there's nothing further to discuss, the witness should be brought in, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Good afternoon, sir. Welcome back to the courtroom. Please sit down and make yourself comfortable.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: I have to remind you that the affirmation to tell the truth you made at the beginning of your testimony still applies.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Tolimir is continuing his cross-examination. Mr. Tolimir.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President. I will like to greet everybody. May God's peace reign in this house, and may God's will be done in these proceedings and not necessarily mine. I greet General Keserovic and I wish him a pleasant stay in our midst.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: [Interpretation] General, sir, yesterday we showed document D176 and that's where we left it off.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we have the same document in e-court, D176. Thank you. Thank you. Can the document please be blown up for the benefit of the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: This document was issued by the Army of the Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: I think there is a technical problem at the moment. The B/C/S version is very small and only on the top of the screen. I hope that problem can be resolved. We have still this problem. Now we can read it. Thank you very much. Mr. Tolimir, please carry on.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: General, sir, this document was issued by the Army of the Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina by its 2nd Corps, or rather, the command of the 2nd corps. They called it the chronology of events surrounding the break through by the 28th Division, and the document says: "Enclosed please find the complete chronology of events from the start of the Chetnik attack on Srebrenica until the break-through carried out by the units of this division and their later consolidation," and so on and so forth. My question to you is this: Did the command of the 2nd Corps of the BiH Army rightly call this document a break-through? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR KESEROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, as I said it yesterday, it was a forced advance or a forced movement. What I had in mind was the fact that when the VRS entered Zepa, the forces had already left the encirclement, but in strategic terms, in view of the fact that there was another front line towards Tuzla, it would be right to call this the break-through of the division from the encirclement.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. My question is this: Did the Main Staff of our Army of the VRS have intelligence and other information to the effect that preparations were under way for the break-through of Muslims from Zepa towards Tuzla, and vice-versa, from Tuzla and Zivinice towards Kakanj, Vlasenica, Srebrenica and Zepa?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR KESEROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There was some intelligence available to us indicating that there could be two-sided offensive activities undertaken by the 2nd Corps on the axis from Tuzla towards Srebrenica, and, at the same time, the division from Srebrenica would try to link up with them and leave the blockade from the enclave. However, I'm not aware of any information about any concrete plans, although there may have been such plans in place.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we see in Court D239, page 2, paragraph 2. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: General, sir, we see this is an intelligence report by the VRS dated the 19th of May. On page 2 that I called up, in paragraph 2 it says: "We have confirmed that the 28th Division is undergoing intense preparations for offensive activities in order to link up with parts of the 23rd Division in the Han Pogled sector. As part of the offensive preparations from the Srebrenica and Zepa enclaves, they have taken possession of important facilities to secure the corridor linking the enclaves and they have partially grouped forces in the western part of the enclaves. They have taken Podravanje, Ljeskovik, Susica, Stublic, Brloznik, Sadilo Cair, Godenje, Ljubomislje, and Gusinac. All of which are outside the so-called demilitarised zone, in order to create better conditions for offensive activities." My question is this: Does this show that they had left the demilitarised zone and that they had taken up facilities outside of the demilitarised zone on the line that I have just described? Does this also confirm the intelligence that we had about their intentions and future activities?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR KESEROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Thank you. This paragraph in this paragraph confirms that, or rather, describes the situation as it was.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you, General, sir. Yesterday and the day before yesterday, you said that you had arrived at the facility in Crna Rijeka and that you didn't find anybody there, that all the officers had left and stayed in the cellar because of the attacks from Zepa and Srebrenica. Do you know when that attack on the command post of the VRS from Srebrenica and Zepa took place?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. McCloskey.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Yes, I think we see the word "cellar" used in a translation here. I'm sure we are talking about the bunker, and since it may get talked about again, I think the -- just want to alert the translation to that. Cellar being, of course, something and that is just something in the bottom of a house.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Tolimir, did you understand the comment of Mr. McCloskey? Were you referring to a bunker or a cellar in your question?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Mr. President, maybe the witness is best suited to answer that. Let me ask him where the Main Staff went and could they all stay in the bunker, the bunker is a very small area.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Maybe the witness could answer.

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR KESEROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was an underground area below Zep hill and that was an area with a footprint of several thousand square metres with a lot of rooms and corridors. It was the war command post for the former JNA. So it was not a bunker but an underground space which was dug into the hill.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you, General, sir.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we now see D145.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: And I will ask you to answer questions about the attacks that was carried out by the forces that had left the demilitarised zone that they had arrived at the command post of the VRS and launched an attack against it. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR KESEROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was not present when that attack took place, but I know that some time in the summer of that same year before Operation Krivaja was launched, there was indeed an attack on the command post. The positions and the facilities of the signals regiment and the protection regiment were attacked on one axis and that was the axis leading to Han Pogled and the waterworks. And the troops suffered major losses. I'm not familiar with any of the details so I wouldn't like to speculate on that.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you, General, sir. Did you see that Han Pogled is mentioned in that intelligence report as the place where the forces from the two directions would link up?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR KESEROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I saw that. I saw that in paragraph 2.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. And now, let's look at this report where it says: "On 23rd June of this year," which was 1995, "at 0200 hours, a unit of approximately 300 soldiers headed out from Srebrenica led by Ibrahim Mandzic, the commander of the 280th Eastern Bosnia Light Brigade and Vejz Sabic, the commander of the 284th Eastern Bosnia Light Brigade," and so and so forth. And then in seconds paragraph, it reads: "In the above sector, this group is to use combat" --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Tolimir, you are reading very fast again, the interpreters and the court recorder hardly can follow. Please slow down while reading. Now the second paragraph you just started with it.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. I apologise for reading fast.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: In the second paragraph it says, and I quote: "In the above sector, this group is to use combat to attract the VRS forces in order to secure safe passage for Naser Oric, who is also moving with a large group from the direction of Kladanj, and will supposedly travel through Pjenovac, Podzeplje and Radava to Srebrenica." Does this indicate that Naser Oric and his forces will head out from Kladanj in order to link up with the forces from Srebrenica? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR KESEROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This is indicated by the report.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Now let's look at the third paragraph: "According to our information, the return of Naser Oric is connected with plans to commence combat operations from the Srebrenica enclave, which, supposedly, is conditioned by the possible taking of the Vis elevation in the Serbian municipality of Kalesija by the Muslim forces in the direction of Kalesija, whereby they would create conditions for further penetration towards the municipality of Sekovici." My question is this: In view of the fact that those groups really arrived, as we will see from further documents and as you learned at the command post and as you, yourself, observed from the activities of the police units and since you did not find any officers there, can you tell us anything about that situation? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR KESEROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The report shows that there were activities on both sides. Both from the protected area of Srebrenica and from the direction of the 2nd Corps and that those were parallel co-ordinated activities aimed at the achievement of the information that we saw before. And that was that active combat would be used in order to provide for the linking up of the two groups of the BiH Army.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. As a soldier, can you tell us whether it is appropriate for demilitarised zone to carry out combat activities against the forces that granted it, the status of demilitarised zone, and that didn't threaten it in military terms? Would you say that that was militarised zone or a demilitarised zone in that case? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR KESEROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was our estimate at the time, based on activities originating from Srebrenica, that it was not demilitarised. Later on that became even more obvious, and ultimately even the international forces and their commanders confirmed that in their reports. It's not only Srebrenica, none of the areas that were supposed to be demilitarised were devoid of forces and weapons.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you, General.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] May I now ask in e-court D193. It's the statement of General Smith and will take a look at what he says about your answer, namely that UNPROFOR itself confirmed that the zones were not demilitarised. It's now on the screen, the statement given on the 14th of August 1996. We need page 9 in B/C/S, paragraph 5.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Let's see what General Smith says about the protected area. But, first of all, let's look at paragraph 2. It says: "On my way back from Srebrenica to Sarajevo, the 7th of March, I met with Mladic at his request." We see from this that before the 7th of March, General Smith had been in Srebrenica to inspect the situation. And that's page 8 in English, paragraph 5. The force commander of UNPROFOR says: "After a series of meetings, I came to the conclusion that Bosnian Serbs had concluded that fighting will be inevitable in the future and some solutions had to be found. The enclaves were too strong and the BH Army within them constituted a clear threat, especially because the Bosnian Serb army felt it was likely they will be confronted with attacks at several fronts." Now, since this is a statement of a general who is also a witness in this case, can you answer this question: Did the UN also have reports that Srebrenica and Zepa enclaves were not demilitarised, and they were, instead, very strong, very well armed?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR KESEROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe that is unequivocal from his statement.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. Do you know whether the United Nations had had taken any steps whatsoever to disarm the enclaves and demilitarise them in keeping with the agreement?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR KESEROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I personally have no information that anything was done. I only know that requests have been made to them to demilitarise these areas but I don't think -- I don't know that anybody actually did anything.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we now look at page 10, last paragraph in Serbian. And that will be page 11 or 9 in English. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: We can see that the general says: "The situation continued to deteriorate. The following week when the BH Army mounted offensives against -- along two axes. They were designed to relieve pressure on Bihac. One attack was at Mount Vlasic which was successful, and the attack against Majevica was not. I concluded that the Bosnian government has no intention of prolonging or extending the COHA," the Cessation of Hostilities Agreement, "after end April." You said you went to the Main Staff to inspect the part of the front line that was attacked by the BH Army and you said you continued on to Bihac. Can you tell us whether the BH Army had violated the Cessation of Hostilities Agreement and started to launch offensives at the time when that agreement was still in place? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR KESEROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Following the decision of the commander of the Main Staff, I went to that area, to the area of that 22nd Vlasic Brigade because in the night between the 18th and the 19th, the 3rd and the 7th Corps attacked that area on a stretch of the front line from the border area of the first Jajic [phoen] Brigade all the way to the Kotor Varos Brigade area along the axis of Paljenik, and that stretch of the front line was occupied at the time and the RS forces were pushed back to the western and north-western slopes of Mount Vlasic. That's where the Bosnian advance was stopped.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. McCloskey.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Could we get a month and a year for that. It's really not evident in the record.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Sir, you said in the night between the 18th and the 19th. Can you give us month and year?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Between the 18th and 19th March, 1995.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Mr. Tolimir.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: It's my fault. I'll continue to quote from this paragraph 10. General Smith says: "I concluded that the Bosnian government had no intention of extending the cessation of hostilities agreement after end April. I met with Dr. Ganic, Mr. Muratovic and General Hajrulahovic on the 22nd of March," the year is 1995, "I was accompanied by Mr. Aguilar. The purpose of this meeting was to assess the political stance of the Bosnian government in relation to the Cessation of Hostilities Agreement following the Bosnian offensive in the Tuzla area. I met with General Delic on the 23rd March in order to gain a clearer understanding of the Tuzla and Travnik areas and assess the potential for maintaining the cease-fire in Bosnia." On the next page he continues: "Throughout April, the situation in Bosnia deteriorated further. The enclaves continued to be squeezed logistically ...," et cetera, et cetera. My question is: Was it the general trend for the Bosnian Army to repair all their tactical positions during cease-fires, to take control of all the strategic features and gain the best possible position in order to occupy, as they said, all of Bosnia-Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR KESEROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: From these activities that we just described, and later the spring offensive in Sarajevo and the offensive on the Ozren-Ozric [phoen] theatre and the activities of the Bosnian corps in other area, led us to the same conclusion. I had not had occasion earlier to see the statement or hear the testimony of General Smith, but this is consistent with what we knew.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Now, bearing in mind the totality of the military situation -- let me repeat for the benefit of the interpreters. Bearing in mind this whole military situation described by General Smith, the force commander of UNPROFOR, where he says that the cease-fires were being violated, was there also a plan by the Bosnian Army that fit into this context, namely to link up the protected areas of Srebrenica and Zepa and bind them with the Zivinice, Kladanj and Tuzla territory?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR KESEROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: All the reports we had and all the activities on their part that we observed led to that conclusion. I don't know any details but I know that we had reports and information about the intention of the Bosnian Army to link up Srebrenica and Zepa enclaves, and to further link them up with Tuzla and perhaps even with another enclave, Gorazde.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you, General.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] May I now ask e-court to display D176 again, page 2. We've already seen page 1. And then I can ask the General about attempts to establish a truce with the enclaves. We'll now see page 2 which describes the chronology. It says: "Brief overview of events in Srebrenica: The 28th Land Force Division and the steps taken." And then it describes everything that was done beginning with 3rd June, 1995, until the 8th of July. Can we scroll down a little so we see the bottom of the page.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Do you see the last paragraph: "Ramiz from Srebrenica notified that the UN had suggested to try to talk to the Chetniks which he refused." Was it the position of the BH Army at the time not to accept any negotiations in or about the demilitarised areas, not even with the UNPROFOR?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR KESEROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is now difficult for me to evaluate the balance of powers, especially in the protected areas relative to the VRS, but generally speaking, the Bosnian Army was far stronger in numbers. It had -- it was already on the move and armed and it outnumbered, simply, the VRS forces.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: We have seen in this last paragraph that Ramiz Becirovic, then Chief of the General Staff, refused negotiations with the Serbs and refused to authorised UN to negotiate with the Serbs because they had already taken control of some favourable positions for their project of linking up the enclaves with Tuzla and other protected areas. Can you tell us if later when the situation became unfavourable for Ramiz, instead of fighting in Srebrenica, he moved with all his forces to break out via Baljkovica with all the military-aged men?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. McCloskey.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Yes. If we could get some idea of what this document is would be helpful. Also, there's no foundation to this question on why the lieutenant-colonel working out of Banja Luka as a military police would know the details of Srebrenica that he learned about in the media. So if he could have a foundational what he knows about these things, I think it would be important before just launching into them from a document that we don't even know what it is.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Tolimir.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Mr. President, the foundation was -- for introducing this document was indicated yesterday when Mr. McCloskey said that the 28th Division ran over the Zvornik Brigade, and that's why I showed this document produced by the BH Army that speaks about the break-out and provides an evaluation of this situation in which they did not even want to negotiate. I thought we needed to see this because this witness was present there for awhile when he visited the command post and when he found out the command post that the forces described here had attacked.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Please, General, upon your arrival to the Main Staff, did you find out that the forces from Srebrenica had attacked the command of the Main Staff of the VRS using active operations from so-called demilitarised zones or zones under the protection of the United Nations? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR KESEROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I found about it one of those days, I'm not sure whether it was immediately upon my arrival, but I did find out that an attack had occurred against the Main Staff itself.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Please, can we have in e-court page 4 of the current document where the 12th of July is discussed, when Mr. Ramiz Becirovic decided to start with the break-through. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Which page is it in English?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It is page 5. Thank you. It's the end of the fourth page in English and then the text continues into the fifth page, but we are interested in second item and I quote:

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: "12 July 1995, in a conversation at 0220 hours, Ramiz reported that he was leaving the enclave along the Urdc-Baljkovica route with his units because Srebrenica had been captured at 1500 hours." And this is my question: From this can we see that Srebrenica surrendered without fighting and that soldiers from Srebrenica went to make their break-through and that they left civilians and population to find shelter in bases including in Potocari?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR KESEROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot see the entire document, but based on this item, it is hard to make any conclusions as to what is going on, but it is clear that chief of the staff of the division is clearly saying that they are setting off to break through outside of the enclave. I don't see any of the rest that you mentioned in this item.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. In your statement -- apologies. In his statement, General Smith said that he was told by General Mladic about how Mladic had been surprised to see empty Srebrenica on his arrival. Did you hear from our soldiers and officers also stories about their surprise with a quick getting into Srebrenica and lack of any resistance?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR KESEROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not have much opportunity to discuss issues with members of troops that entered Srebrenica. What I do remember was that there were several days of preparations and that once UNPROFOR was removed from their check-points, the entry into town itself was relatively easily achieved.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. Please, on this same page in the third paragraph, we see that the 24th Division of the Land Army to put their units in combat readiness for move towards Srebrenica. And then later on we can see, it is in the following paragraph under the locations it says there, the commander of the 28th Division - do you see that - is in Tuzla with a group of officers and he left, and so on and so forth. There is no point for me to read the document now, but one can see that all the units of the 2nd Corps headed that way including Naser Oric with a group of officers that were conducting commander reconnaissance -- command reconnaissance. So can you please tell me whether all this has had the following effect: That they as an armed force managed to overrun the defences of the Zvornik Brigade and link up, starting from Srebrenica with the BH forces in Kladanj and Tuzla? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR KESEROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Considering their numerical strength, and I'm talking about the forces arriving into the area of the Zvornik Brigade, one can say that militarily speaking it was quite logical that the Zvornik Brigade could not stop them.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we please have D155 on our screens to see what the commander of the army had to say about this when addressing his president. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: We see a document issued by the Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina dated 16th July. It is a report on Srebrenica. It was sent via the security organs and among the addressees is also Alija Izetbegovic.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we please see the third page of this document in B/C/S. Thank you. Here on the third page -- it's on the 4th page in English, thank you, Aleksandar. So here we can see the last paragraph marked with number 3. It appeared only now. In the English version, yes, there it is. And there it is stated: "Units of the 28th Division of the Land Army are pulling out of Srebrenica while still fighting. They have remained compact. They have scored success after success in the temporarily-occupied territory. They have inflicted great losses on the aggressor in the course of the fighting. So far, they have eight Chetniks (alive) in captivity. Units of the 28th Division of the Land Army have linked up with the infiltrated units of the 2nd Corps. Their joined forces have continued fighting in the temporarily-occupied territory. It is expected that they will fully link up with these units. Activities are underway to exploit the success of units carrying out the break-through." Thank you, that was the end of the quotation.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: And this is my question: The commander of the BH Army -- and can we please see the last page so we could see the signature block. So the commander of the BH Army, Mr. Rasim Delic, did he assess the break-through operation from Srebrenica and linking up of the forces of Srebrenica and Tuzla as a successful operation?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR KESEROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, this report describes the break-through operation as a success.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone for Mr. Tolimir.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Yesterday, you told us that they didn't have a lot of weapons but can we now see from all these documents that they had enough weaponry to carry out such an operation and to break through the zone of the, at the time, strongest brigade in the area, the Zvornik Brigade? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR KESEROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: On the basis of this report, they obviously had enough weaponry. Yesterday, when I was talking about the issue, I was basing my statements on information according to which in this column of 15.000 people roughly over one-half were only armed, and that's the information I had. And it was on the basis of that that I said that they had just infantry arms. It would be difficult even to imagine that while carrying out a break-through operation they would push or carry artillery weaponry. Whereas the people who were on the front line obviously had all available weapons at their disposal.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. Did you know whether the 28th Division was receiving weapons via air-lifts?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR KESEROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We did have intelligence information about helicopters flying over and heading towards the protected area. The reports also indicated that weapons and ammunition were being brought in.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you, General.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Please, can we have D67 now on our screens. This will confirm what you knew on the basis of reports of the BH Army which will confirm it as fact.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Here we see an interim report sent by the intelligence administration from Sarajevo, BH Army intelligence administration. The date is 13th July, 1995, and it went through the commander of the 1st Corps to the president of the Presidency of the Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina, Alija Izetbegovic, on the 13th of July. So one day after their attempted break-through, they report to him about what they did. In the introduction we can see, I quote: "In view of the situation of our enclaves during the preceding period, the army General Staff has undertaken a series of military activities and procedures to organise the members of the army in the enclaves and prepare them for possible operations, primarily the defence of the existing free territory and planned engagements and preparations for future joint operations and planned operations." Please, on the basis of this, is it obvious that the BH Army was planning joint operations with the forces of Srebrenica throughout the territory of Bosnia-Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR KESEROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, we can see that and this document confirms the following position, at the time when the enclave was allegedly demilitarised, namely before the developments we are talking about here, that weapons had been brought into the enclave via air-lift on many occasions.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you, General. Can we please look at the second line of the report where Alija Izetbegovic is saying 17 helicopter flights were carried out in each of which a helicopter was hit fourth item -- no, I apologise. The third item, in such a manner, we managed to bring back some seriously-injured people, and then the following item: "In preparations for future operation to link up the enclaves we brought in and took back four brigade commanders, two brigade chiefs of staff, and the 26th Division Chief of Staff," that's how it is written here, "the division commander, who was meant to go on the next helicopter flight, did not return after the final flight ended tragically. Naser remained." And this is my question: In this item is it clearly unambiguously stated that he managed to take the commanders from the enclave to Tuzla and back for the purpose of discussing future tasks concerning linking up of enclaves? Have you observed this and how would you comment a report of this sort that the Chief of Staff is sending to his president?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR KESEROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, we can see here that for some reason the commanders went to Tuzla. In the previous item, it is stated that it was in relation to future operations and this also confirms some of our intelligence, according to which air corridors were constantly functioning between Srebrenica and Tuzla.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you, General.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we please turn to the following page. I would like to show General what weapons and ammunition were being supplied from Tuzla to Zepa by plane and then further on from Zepa to Srebrenica via land. The first column represents Zepa; second, Srebrenica; and the third is total. Can we please have the following page in English where -- yes, we see this overview here as well. The following page, please, where one can see the signature to see who was it who issued this document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Tolimir, we have it on the screen, please continue.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: General, helicopter flights, could they have come unobserved to the demilitarised zone without being observed by the UN forces whose task it was to make sure that the enclave is demilitarised? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR KESEROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, they certainly could not because the check-points, and the check-points UNPROFOR troops were deployed and VRS forces were around the enclave. If the Serbian soldiers could observe this, then the UN observers should have been able to do the same.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would like to call up D16 in e-court.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: And while we are waiting for it to be shown, I have to say for the record that this document was issued by the Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina by the General Staff of the BiH Army. It was sent from Kakanj to the command of the 2nd Corps to OG 8 Srebrenica and to the command of the 1st Zepa Brigade. Please, let's look at the 6th line from the top of the page and you will see that the report was sent to their commanders. It says: "On the 16th of February, 1995, the aggressor filed a request with UNPROFOR to declare Zepa a non-demilitarised zone, with the following rationale." I don't want to go on reading, but I would like to say that they repeat everything that General Mladic sent the UNPROFOR command as his objections. What follows is an order and under 1 it says: "Bring units of OG 8 to full combat readiness." Under bullet point 2, they say that a co-ordinated action should be organised. Under bullet point 4, it says the helicopter has to be camouflaged. UNPROFOR was not allowed to inspect and therefore the instructions for dealings with UNPROFOR. My question is this: Bearing in mind the information that we sent to UNPROFOR, bearing in mind that we requested for the zone to be demilitarised, can you tell us, do you know whether any steps were taken by UNPROFOR to demilitarise those zones to be disarmed and for the weapons to be returned which would have stopped us from doing it by force? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR KESEROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not aware of any steps that may have been done to that effect.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we now look at P1011 [Realtime transcript read in error "P10111"] in e-court. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: What we see here is the agreement on complete cessation of hostilities. In the first paragraph the agreement reads: "Following the cease-fire agreement signed on the 23rd December 1994, the parties agree to a complete cessation of hostilities with effect from 1200 hours on the 1st of January, 1995, along all lines of confrontation. This agreement will be in effect for an initial period of four months, subject to renewal under the these same conditions by agreement of the parties." My question: Do you know if this agreement was honoured by the Muslims, or rather, is it during that time that most of their hostilities took place against our forces that were in the area?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR KESEROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Please continue your answer.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We have already spoken about this period, and we said that during that period, during that winter and early spring, this cease-fire agreement was not complied with in many parts of the combat area, for example, on Mount Vlasic. And according to what I know, it was not honoured in the zone of the 30th Division from Kupres to Donji Vakuf, and the same situation prevailed in Bihac front line in Mount Ozren and the territories around Doboj. There were a lot of places where the agreement was not honoured.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Tolimir, could you please repeat the number of the document because it's wrongly recorded.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President. The document number is P1011.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: In the second paragraph, it says: "The cessation of hostilities will be supervised and monitors by UNPROFOR through the establishment of Joint Commissions." Can you tell us anything you know about the fact whether they prevented activities against the units of the VRS in which you participated at the time?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR KESEROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: According to my experience which does not have to be the experience of others, the international forces, at least from the point of view of the VRS, left the area in case of any incidents and they justified that by security reasons.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. Do you know whether UNPROFOR also left UNPA zones in Croatia before Croatia or its army launched its attack on those zones?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR KESEROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot testify to that. I was not a firsthand witness, but it is a historical fact before Operation Storm and Flash began and before that in 1993 before operations started to liberate Maslenica and the hinterland of Zadar, the forces that had been in Croatia would leave the area before those operations were launched.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you, sir. In the transcript on page 23, I believe, I don't know if I recorded the page number well, actually, it was on page 18, line 2 of the transcript the day before yesterday, you were asked whether that would include UNPROFOR and NATO. You were talking about counter-intelligence activities and protection measures, and you were asked whether those included UNPROFOR and NATO. On page 18, line 2, and on line 4, you answered that it was probably so. My question is this: Did we have any specific information about abuses among UNPROFOR or individuals there and that information was conveyed through them from one side to another?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR KESEROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There was intelligence to that effect, to the effect that information was conveyed about the two sides, and the bad experience probably resulted in our concern about the intentions of the international forces. We were very cautious about them.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. McCloskey, you raised one second earlier than Mr. Gajic. Mr. McCloskey.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: We got in English, "Did we have information," and of course we need to know what he means by that. "We" could mean: We, the VRS; we, the Main Staff; you and I. So it's not a very helpful way to ask a question. The answer was very clear, there was intelligence that, but it doesn't really answer the question because it's impossible to answer "we" because we don't know who "we" is. So if you could be more particular with that, I think it would be helpful.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Gajic.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, I would like to say for the transcript that that was recorded on the 10th of May, 2011, page 13876.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: This is the updated numbering of the transcript of the day before yesterday. Thank you. Judge Nyambe has a question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE NYAMBE
utterances.text: Yes, I just wonder if you could clarify for me, at page 23, in lines 14 to 19, at the end of those lines you've stated there were a lot of places where the agreement was not honoured, meaning the cease-fire agreement. Who or which parties did not honour the cease-fire agreement? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Tolimir's question was about the BiH Army which means that I was referring to the BiH Army in my answer.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE NYAMBE
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Tolimir, if I recall correctly, you have used the term "we" several times yesterday and today when you put questions to the witness. Taking me account the remark of Mr. McCloskey, indeed it would be helpful to identify exactly what you are meaning. Carry on, please.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. Thank you, Mr. McCloskey. When I say "we," I mean the VRS. I apologise for the feeling that it was both myself and the General, the two of us were members of the same service. In my future questions and answers, I will try to be very clear for the record. I would like to call up D188 in e-court. Thank you. We can see the document on the screen. We see a document before us which says that UNPROFOR conveyed information about the VRS to the BiH Army. Let's just read the beginning of the document. The document was issued by the Gorazde state security sector. It was signed by the chief --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Before you continue, is there an English translation? In your list of documents to be used with this witness, you indicated that there is a translation. Mr. Tolimir, could you clarify that, or Mr. Gajic.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President. We thought that the document was translated because it was used during the examination of General Smith. It seems we were wrong, it hasn't been translated apparently.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: I think it's marked for identification. Mr. Gajic.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Mr. President, this is an exhibit which was marked for identification not only because there is no -- there was no translation during Mr. Smith's testimony. As far as I know, we have not received a translation yet. As soon as we have it, it will be uploaded in e-court.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Please continue.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: We can see that the document was drafted by the state security sector in Gorazde. That was a territory under the BiH Army control. The date is 22nd July, 1995. That document was submitted to their superiors. In the first paragraph, it says: "We inform you that on the 1st of July, 1995, in the evening hours, we were invited by the commander of UNPROFOR in Gorazde, Colonel John Riley, for a short meeting. He explained that he was prepared to offer to us some of the intelligence that he had obtained in a telephone conversation with General Smith." This document therefore confirms that the UNPROFOR commander in Gorazde collated intelligence to the Muslim side. My question is this: If the security organs of one army receive intelligence and information that there may be spy activities against them on the part of UNPROFOR and NATO, are they duty-bound to draft a plan of counter-intelligence activity against such an organisation?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR KESEROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, according to our rules we had that obligation. And it was the counter-intelligence group that focused on those activities, if at all possible.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. My question is this: Was that in keeping with the rules and laws which were in force and that we were duty-bound to comply with, and when I say "we," I mean the Main Staff and the intelligence administration or members of the VRS in general?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR KESEROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that was in keeping with the rules and laws.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we now see D189, please. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Now we can see D189. It's also a document from the state security service in Gorazde dated 18 June which says, I quote: "Regarding your request from your dispatch, please be informed that with a view to verifying reports received earlier we had a discussion with Colonel Roger from the BritBat. In that conversation, Roger confirmed what we had heard earlier from Officer Allen and said that the aggressor had been seen regrouping with forces two or three brigades strong in the broad area of Trnovo. He also said that this should not be of any concern to us because in his estimate it was -- it involved 1.500 to 1.600 aggressor troops." Now, did you have any knowledge about UNPROFOR members sharing information with one or another side?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR KESEROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This document seems to confirm that.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Pursuant to laws and regulations, would it be the duty of the counter-intelligence service to act against such persons?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR KESEROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we see D237. Could we rotate the document so the witness can read it.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: This is an intelligence report from the Main Staff of the VRS dated 30th March, 1995. We are looking at paragraph 2 which says -- it's the next page in English: "According to reports from reliable sources, the Americans are providing Muslims with intelligence about VRS units. UNPROFOR and NATO continue to threaten with bombardment of VRS positions and installations in the event that the VRS mounting a counter-attack to crush the Muslim offensive carries out an attack against Muslim enclaves, although there is no agreement about that at the UN Security Council." My question is: Were the Americans able to gather the most information about the Army of Republika Srpska and other parties to the conflict because they had drones of all kinds flying over all theatres of war on the pretext that they were doing it for their requirements and UNPROFOR and NATO.

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR KESEROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's quite likely that some of the satellites covering this territory were active non-stop and they were able to have such information.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Tolimir, we must have our first break now. Before we break, I would like to clarify two dates. You said in relation to this document, this is an intelligence report from the Main Staff of the VRS dated 30th of March, 1995. In your list, you were indicating it's the 31st of March. It is not very legible, but we see handwriting on the top of this document from the 31st of March. The document itself, it's hardly legible, just for the record. The other date which is -- seems to be unclear is the previous document from the 21st of July. You said on page 27, line 20, the date is 22nd of July. Now, it should be the 2nd of July instead of 22nd. We have to adjourn and resume quarter past 4.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Tolimir, please carry on.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President. Thank you for -- [Microphone not activated]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Your microphone.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you for noticing the dates on these documents. The date is 31 March, not the 30th. You can see that on the last page where the encrypting officer signed it. And on the second document, it's the 2nd, not the 22nd. Could we have this document D188 and D189 dated 18 June admitted or marked for identification pending translation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: They are both marked for identification on two reasons: One is the lack of translation, and the other was that the witness, Sir Smith, was not able to identify these documents and couldn't testify about its content. I think the situation, this is my personal impression, has not changed yet because the witness says, yes, if I read this it seems to indicate something. He was not able to identify the documents as well.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President. Please, could we now display 1D196. This document, 196 is D196. We received something else.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: The reason is that you indicated the wrong number, 1D196. But now you are asking for D196, that is fine.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President. I will try not to make these mistakes in future.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: This is a document from the Main Staff of the Army of Republika Srpska dated 24 February 1995. It's a protest addressed by General Mladic to the command of the UNPROFOR in Zagreb to the attention of General de Lapresle and to the command of the UNPROFOR in Sarajevo to the attention of General Smith. This protest, General Mladic says, I'm quoting from paragraph 1: "On 23rd February, 1995, around 2010 hours another freight aircraft landed on the auxiliary runway of Tuzla airport carrying weapons and military equipment and escorted by two fighter planes of NATO which secured and protected it in flight and during unloading. Regrettably, this has happened more than once lately before the eyes and ears of NATO and UNPROFOR forces in the air and at the Tuzla airport who do not do anything to prevent these violations of the relevant UN Security Council resolutions banning import of weapons and military equipment." My question is: Is it the case that our forces frequently addressed protests to the UNPROFOR over the arming of Muslims, especially 1994 and 1995, with the assistance of the UNPROFOR and NATO forces deployed in Bosnia?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR KESEROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I knew that protests were sent and that in direct contact and talks this issue was raised repeatedly.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we now display -- or rather, could we have this document admitted first and then let us display P1430.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: The document we just had on the screen was already marked for identification pending translation. We are still waiting for the translation.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: This document speaks of an incident like the one you mentioned. This was written by the UNPROFOR staff for Bosnia-Herzegovina, the author is Colonel Baxter, and it was submitted on the 6th of March, 1995, in the form of minutes of the meeting between General Smith and General Mladic. In paragraph 1, we read: "Today at Jahorina ski resort south of Pale, a meeting took place between General Smith and General Mladic. The meeting was organised at the invitation of General Mladic. This is the first occasion, in the memory of HQ BHC, that Mladic has been the instigator of a meeting. The invitation was issued during a telephone conversation the previous day when General Smith obtained General Mladic's clearance for a resupply of DutchBat in Srebrenica. The meeting lasted two and a half hours. Major-General Tolimir attended throughout," and so on and so forth. Now, below on the same page, paragraph 2 (b): "Mladic alleged the use of Tuzla airfield for the supply of arms to the BiH Army covered by NATO. General Smith stated that he was satisfied that NATO was not resorting -- sorry, not escorting or was in any way associated with the alleged landings of aircraft at Tuzla. General Smith reported that UNPROFOR will continue to observe the area and report sightings to NATO as part of Operation Deny Flight. Mladic acknowledged that aircraft had been observed and sighted." My question is: Does this confirm what you said, namely that in direct contact the problems related to the supply of weapons to Muslims covered by NATO and UNPROFOR was frequently raised?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR KESEROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, this report confirms that this was one of the topics.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Did we in the final stages of the war -- I mean me in the Main Staff. I apologise for again saying we. Did we, the intelligence and security administration, receive reports that in the final stages of the war NATO forces together with BH Army forces and the Croatian Army would attack the territory and the Army of Republika Srpska? Do you know that we had such information?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR KESEROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, we had such reports. They reached also the forward command post in Bosanska Krajina.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. Seeing that you had visited the forward command post of General Milovanovic, were there any NATO and Croatian Army operations against the VRS in that part of our territory?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR KESEROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I cannot speak to any direct operations by NATO forces, but I can confirm that I personally observed operations mounted by the Croatian Army, both their land forces and their aviation.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Do you know whether NATO attacked installations of Republika Srpska in those final stages in July and August?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR KESEROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I had forgotten about that. In Republika Srpska, all radio relay hubs were destroyed, such as on Mount Kozara, at Svinjar, Mount Majevica, Ozren, Kmur, Leotar. I don't know all the places. In any case, all communication centres and radio relay hubs were destroyed.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. As a war time commander in various units ranking from battalion to Chief of Staff of a corps, what can you tell us about what the communication system represent for maintaining the full combat readiness of units?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR KESEROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can give you an illustration. We would call it the throbbing vein of any army or any defence system.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Would then NATO operations against this throbbing vein, would that be something that would have influence on the positions of VRS in relation to Croatian Army and BH Army, in those parts of the battle-field where you were present?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR KESEROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it would and it did.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Could you just briefly tell us in what way, which positions were lost at the time in Republika Srpska, what VRS lost of the positions that they had held before that?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR KESEROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: An area covering about 11 municipalities in western Krajina: Grahovo, Glamoc, Drvar, Petrovac, Krupa, Kljuc, Mrkonjic Grad, Sanski Most, Jajce and Donja Vakuf. We lost all these municipalities within a period of two months of joint operations by NATO forces against radio relay, hubs and Croatian Army land operations.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. If the commander of the Main Staff of Republika Srpska would receive intelligence such as this, namely that NATO is assisting in arming Muslims, that UNPROFOR is protecting this process of ABiH arming, would the commander then be justified in sending intelligence officers to examine the situation which would later help him in negotiations?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR KESEROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, that's one of the focuses of the intelligence work, namely protection of units and facilities, infrastructure facilities in the army and in the Republika Srpska as such.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. Since throughout 1995, as we have seen in this document recently, should have introduced truce and in -- cease of hostilities for a long period of time. Can you tell me whether the commander of the army according to regulations could have insisted that intelligence and counter-intelligence activities should be focused on those issues? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR KESEROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The commander of the Main Staff is in any case authorised to take all measures using intelligence forces at his disposal to protect intelligence and counter-intelligence in both the troops and the territory.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. On page 10 of the transcript from two days ago, line 18, I don't know which page but my legal assistant will surely tell me, the Prosecutor showed document P01112 which was instruction on command and control. On page 11 in the first line you told us that you haven't seen that document while you were in the VRS.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would like to ask for this document, P01112, to be put on the screens so that we can see what is in it. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: We see this instruction of the Main Staff of the VRS dated 24th of October that was used during the direct examination. We will not go into any further details except saying that at the time, and this is on page 11, lines 23 to page 12, there you said that there is a problem with the percentages, that it shouldn't be 80/20. Instead, it should be two-thirds, one-third, and one-third should be for the staff-related tasks, not 20, but 16 [as interpreted]. And this is my question: The commander of the Main Staff of the VRS who is commanding by using measures and methods and gives orders to the organs of the military police, can he issue an order that during periods of truce and when there is an increased presence of international elements in the zone, can he order that the number of intelligence officers be increased at expense of those who are engaged in command and staff activities? Is that his right?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR KESEROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: If you remember when I was talking about the percentage, I also stated that I'm not sure that I don't know what were the reasons for the decisions of the commander of the Main Staff. I didn't know about what you've just told me now, but that it was customary and it was also stated in the rules that the distribution be two-thirds, one-third, but if there were reasons, of course, the commander could have changed the ratio any which way he wanted.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you, General. During the examination-in-chief, you were also asked whether the JNA rules were applied in the VRS. And this is my question: The JNA rules concerning the activities of the military police, the security service, and command and control, were they something that could also be used in the VRS in the same way as they had been applied before? What was missing there and was there any reason for change?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR KESEROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: They could have been used because the continuity of application of the rules was there, and with the change of conditions, some of the rules were changed but they were mainly taken over and used as they were. And, as far as I know, all the parties in the area continued using all rules, and even in other spheres, the Criminal Code and so forth. The problem was that the new laws were not drafted yet after the changes in the political and governmental system, but the old rules applied until new rules would be in effect.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Please, can we please have D203 on our screens.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: This is rule of service in the security organs of the Socialist Federative Republic of Yugoslavia. We'll see it on the screen soon. Can we turn it around. And this is my question: Were these rules of service used in the VRS while you were a member of the VRS?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR KESEROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can you please turn to page 30 in English. Yes, 30 in the English and in Serbian page 30.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Let's see what the rules say about how it should be applied in practice and during war time.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we please show page 30 in Serbian. Item 84. I apologise, it's page 24 in e-court. I made a mistake.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Here we can see item 85, "Work of Security Organs During War Time," and it says: "In war, security organs act in accordance with the provisions of these rules and other rules and regulations that regulate the work of security organs adapting their own activity, methods, and means of work to the war time conditions." And this is my question: General, even in peacetime did we have -- did we in peacetime get an open opportunity, an option to act in accordance with these rules?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR KESEROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: In item number 2, we can read the following: "In combat activities, security organs organise and implement methods of counter-intelligence security and participate, within the framework of their competence, in the organisation of security measures and self-protection of commands, units, institutions ...," and so on and so forth. End of quotation. This is my question: Security organs in war time, were they authorised to carry out measures of counter-intelligence support for units, institutions?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR KESEROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, according to the regulations.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. These rules, did they apply also in various republics that were part of former Yugoslavia, both in peacetime and in war time? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR KESEROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, they applied throughout the former state and therefore all of its republics. For the defence and in terms of application of the rules before us, there was no difference between republics. The only thing that mattered was Socialist Federative Republic of Yugoslavia.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you, General.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we please move now to item 87. It is the last item in the Serbian version. Can we please turn to the following page in the English. Yes, thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: There it is stated: "Security organs familiarise the competent military officer with the counter-intelligence situation and, on the basis of the conclusions of the evaluation under item 86, paragraph 1 of these rules, recommend counter-intelligence support measures. In the process of the work of commands, units, institutions, and staffs of the armed forces in preparing and carrying out combat activities, at the request of a competent military officer, security organs recommend necessary security measures and the use of the military police." And my question to you is the following: Can you tell us who is the competent officer in relation to security organs in VRS to whom assessments and estimates were to be recommended and submitted?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR KESEROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Exclusively the commanders.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. At all levels of command, can you tell us whether security organs were briefing commanders about counter-intelligence assessments and proposed and recommended measures and use of military police for the purpose of protection of units, institutions, and staff, and did commanders authorise them and approve their recommendations?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR KESEROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Security organs participated at all levels in relation to recommending measures concerning the use of military police, if there was military police within the unit, and my experience was that commanders would mostly accept the recommendation, sometimes change it a bit, and very seldom turn it down.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you, General.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Let us turn to page 5 in Serbian, page 6 in the English, on e-court to see what was the scope of activities of the security organs.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: I will then put the question to you. Thank you. Please read to yourself item number 1. There's no point in me reading it out to you, and then I will ask you a question. And this is my question but I will wait for you to read the text first. I apologise. So this is my question: Security organs within the VRS, were these organs in charge of security of the Republika Srpska, its army, its institutions, and its territory?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR KESEROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, they were in charge of state security, and within the system of defence one of the basic laws was the one about security organs which implied armed forces security organs as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. I apologise for not having prepared a constitution to show you, but it was shown to you during the examination-in-chief. My question is this: When it comes to the constitution of the Republika Srpska, was it in any way limiting upon the work of the security organs and the state security organs, or rather, did they have the same tasks that they would have had no matter what the constitutional order was? What I'm saying is that they were duty-bound to protect the constitutional order? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR KESEROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: If general terms, every constitution irrespective of the type of the security system elements bounds them to protect the constitutional order of that state and the principle values of that state or its elements, the territory, the population and the political system or the political order that exists in the state.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. Bearing in mind what you have just told us, did the constitution of the Republika Srpska limit the application of the rules from the former JNA governing the work of the security services within the army and the institutions?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR KESEROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I know, there were no restrictions.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we now move to page 6 in the English version and page 6 in the Serbian version. We would like to look at paragraph 6, or rather, bullet point 6, paragraph 2, "The tasks of the security organs."

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Now we can see that. I am not going to read from the text. In the examination-in-chief, you were asked about this paragraph, you were asked about your tasks and activities. I'm just going to read the first sentences in each of the paragraphs: "6(a), The detection, tracking and prevention of intelligence activities and other activities of foreign military intelligence. 6(b), The detection and prevention of hostile activities by individuals groups or organisations against armed forces and members of the arms forces. 6(c), The implementation of measures and operations of counter-intelligence protection." Let's move on to the following page, page 7 in English. We want to see 6(2)(b), which is: "Prescribing measures of protection and self-protection. (c), planning the training of permanent reserve force." And now let's look at (d) where it says: "In professional terms, the control of the military police units and then actions that precede the commission of a crime and criminal proceedings" --

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR KESEROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe that there has been a mistake. I'm looking at page 12 instead of page 7 or 8. I'm looking at a different text on the screen.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we see page 13 in Serbian. I'm not going to repeat again. Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you, General Keserovic. My question based on what we have just read out is this: When it comes to the control of the military police, was it only in professional terms that the security organs were in charge of the military police as it is stated in bullet point 7(d)?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR KESEROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, only in professional terms and I believe that in the previous examination I said exactly that.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. Could you please explain for the benefit of the Trial Chamber what is the difference between the professional relationship and the command relationship within a unit or within a command of a military organisation? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR KESEROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: A command relationship is a relationship which implies subordination and an exclusive right by the commander to use a military police unit or rather to give it orders and tasks as he would to any other unit on the strength of that unit. That is the relationship between the commander of the unit and the commander of the military police unit. There is a direct link between the two. In terms of a professional control over military police units, this implies activities with regard to the staffing of the unit, training, it's preparedness for the execution of policing duties, the duty service, planned control of the military police services and other tasks and duties which fall out of the scope of command or issuing orders for the direct use of that unit.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you, General, sir.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we now look at page 10 in English and page 9 in Serbian.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: We want to see the part about which you were asked yesterday, and that was why did we share responsibility within a single organisation. Let's look at a bullet point 16, "Management of security organs." I'm going to read bullet point 6 [as interpreted] where it says: "The security organ is directly subordinated to the commanding officer of the command unit, institution, or staff of the armed forces in whose strength it is placed in the establishment, and it is responsible to that officer for its work ..." My question: Were security organs in the security administration of the Main Staff of the VRS subordinated to the commanding officer of the unit or institution or staff or to the chief of their service? Who were they subordinated to in military terms?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR KESEROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In military terms, they were subordinated to the commander. In this particular case the officers in the sector for intelligence and security were subordinated to the commander of the Main Staff. That was in military terms. In professional terms and for some professional tasks, that fell within the scope of the work of the security organs, primarily counter-intelligence. They were subordinated to the officer of the professional unit, in this case it would be the sector for security and intelligence.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Mr. Keserovic, could you tell us, please, whether that relationship of subordination in professional terms also implied the subordination to the superior officer, military commander who approved any measures ordered?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR KESEROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, certainly. This means that the activities of the organisational unit for security or the security sector or the security administration or the security section were planned, and those plans were approved by the officer or the commander of the unit on whose strength any of those institutions or units existed.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. Since we are talking about very specific use of measures, methods, and means of work, I would like us to look at bullet point 17, and then I'm going to ask you to answer a question because during the examination-in-chief you were asked about methods and means.

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR KESEROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: When it comes to the application of different methods and means of work or combined application of methods of work, in war time the commander of the Main Staff, or, if it has been otherwise stipulated, it can also be the minister of defence would be the one who approved individual use of some particular methods. Under peacetime conditions, and that applies today, the approval of the use of special methods is within the purview of the courts. This means that none of the methods or means of work of the security organs can be approved by the commander of that unit or applied by the commander of that unit.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. Did the same regulations apply during the war? In other words, that the commander could not do anything in that sense without the approval of the superior officer?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR KESEROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, the same rules applied.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. Who was the superior officer of all security organs in the VRS in keeping with the rules and regulations? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR KESEROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The commander of the Main Staff of the VRS.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. Could you please tell us, you were asked about covert methods, was anybody in a position to approve the application of a covert method without a prior approval by a court or in war time by prior approval of the superior commander?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR KESEROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, that cannot be done legally.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Can we look at bullet point 22, which says: "The senior officer of a command unit, institution, or staff of the armed forces supervises the work of subordinate security organs according to the general regulations ..." Who was the superior officer in the commands of the brigades and the Main Staff? Who was in charge of managing security organs at those levels? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR KESEROVIC [Resumed]
