utterances.text: The unit commander.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we now look at page 10 in Serbian and page 11 in English.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Let's look at the other parts of bullet point 22 dealing with management and control. The second paragraph reads, and I quote: "The control application of methods and techniques used by the security organs is carried out by the commanding officer pursuant to the previous rule." Who was it in the VRS that was the superior officer pursuant to Article 17 of these regulations?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR KESEROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was the commander of the Main Staff.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. Can we look at bullet point 23. This bullet point speaks about professional control and management of the military police units. Let's read the first paragraph, we are talking about professional relationship. And in the second paragraph of the same bullet point it reads, and I'm quoting: "When it comes to the control of the military police units, the commanding -- the security organ officer under paragraph 1 of this item has the same rights and duties as officers of arms and services of commands, units, institutions, and staffs of the armed forces in managing units of the arms and services of those commands, units, institutions, and staffs." My question is this: Was the security organ in possession of bigger rights than the chief of artillery in respect of all the officers who were members of the artillery units? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR KESEROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. All organs of arms and services in the army had the same rights and that relationship, professional relationship vis-a-vis units that belonged to those arms or services. This same applied to the security organs. He had the same rights as, for example, the chief of the artillery, engineers, communications and others.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. Since you were a commander of military police units and since you trained military police men and officers in those units and later on in the service, you were the most responsible person for all that, could you tell us whether the same rules were prescribed for the officers in the military police and for the professional organs in the military police, and is that highlighted in the rules governing the work of the military police, that is that they had the same rights as the other officers of arms and services?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR KESEROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, they had the same rights.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we now look at page 12 in Serbian and page 15 in English. We are interested in paragraph 32, or rather, bullet point 32, paragraph 4.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: We can see it now. This is the last paragraph on page 23. It's the last paragraph under bullet point 32. Thirty-two, last paragraph, and I'm reading now, and I quote: "When the approval of the officer under item 17 of these rules cannot be obtained in time, and when the" -- I misspoke. I didn't say 17. "And when the situation urgently demands it, the application of methods and means of security organs work may be decided upon by the senior officer of an army's security organ or an equal officer of a JNA security organ or the senior officer of the security organ or a Territorial Defence staff of a republic or autonomous province. But he is obliged to notify, without any delay, the officer under item 17 of these rules of the measures taken ..." My question is this: In case of an emergency, if a method had to be applied and if the commander was not there as the responsible officer, who would have had the right to approve the use of such methods and to inform him immediately thereafter about the application and the results of the method that was applied?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR KESEROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In this case, an equivalent to the command of the army was the VRS, and the chief of the sector for security and intelligence had the right to apply measures temporarily but he was also duty-bound to inform thereafter the commander.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you, General. Can we look at number 48 in this rule. It's page 20 in English; page 19 is the beginning in Serbian, point or paragraph 49. We are reading it because it was raised in cross-examination. In keeping with the responsibilities and duties as established by the law and regulations, the authorised commanding officer of security organs is responsible for performing the tasks within the field of competence of security organs as designated by his commanding officer regardless of whether these tasks form part of the tasks normally executed at the establishment post they occupy. My question is: When your superior officer ordered you to go and carry out strictly military tasks, did you go to do that and did you later report back to him regardless of the fact that these tasks did not fall strictly within the -- your field of work in the establishment post you occupied?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. McCloskey.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: This is a vague on an important point. If we could get who the superior officer is or what position he holds, then the answer would have some meaning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: It's a very compound question, if you see that in the transcript. Would you be in a position to rephrase your question and make it a bit more specific, Mr. Tolimir?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Mr. Keserovic, who was your superior officer at the Main Staff?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR KESEROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: My immediate superior in the security administration was Colonel Beara, but if we look at the Main Staff as a whole, then the commander of the Main Staff, militarily speaking, was the commander.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Were you in the security administration the authorised commanding officer of security organs?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR KESEROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Gajic.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr President, I would like to ask Mr. Tolimir to repeat the question because on page 50, we see "the authorised commanding officer."

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Were you the authorised officer, senior officer over security organs at the security administration?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR KESEROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I was as envisaged by the rules of service of security organs.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Did your establishment position involve command over combat units?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR KESEROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Did your senior officer send you to an assignment where you would have to be involved in commanding?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR KESEROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There have been situations when it was suggested that I take command over a group of units.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. McCloskey.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Sorry ... [Microphone not activated]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Microphone doesn't work. What happened to you?

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: It's after 5.15, maybe they are cutting me off which sometimes is a good idea.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Now it's working.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: I think I'm okay. It's just come on. Again, same objection for vagueness, because it's, "Did your senior officer...," and it may be translation, but as a lieutenant-colonel he has got more senior officers than, you know, he has got hundreds of them. So we need to know what -- who he is talking about, or, at least, the position that he is talking about because there are a lot of generals that can order him. So this doesn't help us when the question is phrased like this.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Tolimir, could you please be, again, a bit more specific.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: My question was, and it was clear to everyone: Were you given that task from -- were you given that task by your senior officer from the intelligence administration or your senior officer who was the superior of all the organs?

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Same objection: vague. What task now? We don't even know what task he is talking about.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: We will hear the answer and perhaps then Mr. Tolimir should clarify it. Sir, did you understand the question? Please clarify.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Stop, please. We don't receive interpretation at the moment. Could you please repeat your answer.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I think I can answer. The thing is that a task to take command over units was not received by me from security organs but from the competent commander. In this case that we are discussing, it's General Tolimir -- sorry, the Main Staff commander, General Mladic. General Mladic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: It's really confusing.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: I think I know what he is talking about, but the question didn't give him -- doesn't identify the task and he doesn't identify the task. So if somebody could identify the task, we'll all be fine, I think.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Tolimir.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: General, since these things are difficult for some people to understand, I will put it in several questions and you give me the best possible answers you can. At the command post, did you receive orders and a task to go to Bratunac to integrate command over several brigades, and who gave you -- who issued you with that task?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR KESEROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Originally, I was given that task by the commander of the Main Staff, General Mladic.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. Did he order his operations officer to also write an order to that effect after notifying you verbally?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR KESEROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He did. He ordered General Miletic to write an order to that effect.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Did Mr. McCloskey show you that order in both of the variants during examination-in-chief?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR KESEROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I have had occasion to see it.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Did General Mladic later change his orders and tell you to just go and see what the situation is and report back to him?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR KESEROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Did you follow that order given you by the military commander?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR KESEROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Therefore, does the military commander have the right to also engage officers from the security administration to carry out whatever tasks he designates?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR KESEROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The commander of the Main Staff has the right to engage every member of any unit under his command.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: As a soldier, did you carry out the task given you by your Commander-in-Chief?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR KESEROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, on that day I executed the task I had been given to the extent possible.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Did you report back along the chain of command as to what you had observed that day on the ground and the situation and the condition of our units?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR KESEROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't think I made a report in writing, but I believe I informed General Miletic, I think, at the operation centre, about what I had seen and what was going on.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Did that end your engagement on military tasks and did you then return to your normal work envisaged by your establishment post in your security organ?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR KESEROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, I believe we have now cleared up the matter. If anything remains outstanding, Mr. McCloskey can take it up in redirect.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: It was a very good idea to split up the compound question and now we have received clear answers. Thank you very much for that. Please carry on.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Look at paragraph 50. In case of lack of diligence in carrying out tasks in their field of work or failure to comply or violation of the provisions of this rule, the officers serving in security organs shall be held responsible in keeping with the general rules. Now, my question is: If you had refused or failed to carry out the tasks given you by your military commander, would you have been held responsible for that?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR KESEROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I believe we discussed that before. I would have been held responsible under general regulations depending on the gravity of the violations of general rules and laws. Sometimes it would be disciplinary proceedings and in some cases it could even be criminal proceedings.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you, General.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we now move to page 22 in Serbian and 23 in English to look at the powers of the security administration of the Federal Ministry of Defence [as interpreted], and, in this case, of the Main Staff. We are looking for paragraph 57 in Serbian, too, because now we are looking at 74. We need to go a few pages back. It's page 16 in Serbian in e-court.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's correction: It's not the Federal Ministry of Defence, it's the security administration.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Paragraph 57: "The security administration of SSNO, (hereinafter security administration) shall perform its duties as prescribed by these rules and other regulations. The security administration provides professional management for security organs in JNA commands, units and institutions according to the provisions of these rules and organises and directs their work of importance for security." First of all, tell me, does the security administration of the level of the Main Staff have the same powers and authority as the security administration of the Federal Ministry of Defence in the former Yugoslavia?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR KESEROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Since the whole rules were taken over, the rights and responsibilities have also been translated or taken over, adopted into our rules.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Did you have the same rights and responsibilities, only in professional terms, to command security organs in lower level units?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR KESEROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, only in our professional terms.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. Now look at 58. The first sentence reads: "The security administration provides specialised direction and co-ordination for the work of security organs of the Territorial Defence relating to counter-intelligence matters and the counter-intelligence protection of members of the armed forces." Now, this professional direction in counter-intelligence tasks and affairs, does it apply to all the work carried out by security organs.

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR KESEROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, the security administration directs all the organs down the chain, and on lower levels it goes through the commander of the security organ. In the corps, it goes through the chief of the security section of the corps.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we please now see item 67 which is on page 18 in the Serbian version and on page 25 in the English version. Item 67 of these rules.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: And my question is the following: Was the security administration in charge of professional training and improvement of skills of members of the armed forces, and by that I mean the military police and security service members within the armed forces?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR KESEROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I believe this question was already put when they organise education, participates in programming and monitors the conduct of training. This is what the security administration is in charge of.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Keserovic, let us now look at item 85 of the rules. No, I apologise, it's not 85, it's 96. That's the last page. And here in item 96 it is stated: "The chief of the security administration is hereby authorised to give necessary explanations for the preparation and implementation of these rules." And my question is: All unclear provisions concerning professional view of the military police organs, was that something that could be issued by the chief of the security administration?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR KESEROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, he could provide explanations and to interpret the rules.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. Since you went through various levels of command within the army, the brigade, the corps, always in military police, could you tell us: Did the police forces have chemical agents for suppressing rebellion or unrest, and did the military police at all levels have such chemical abilities?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR KESEROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: At certain levels in battalions of military police there were units, organisational units of company strength that were called anti-terrorist companies. These companies had at their disposal so-called action chemical agents in packages that were ready-made for manual use, mostly it was tear gas, and occasionally there would be a special rifle available for a bullet that was -- that included tear gas. So in some units, and this is the legacy of the JNA, the military police had means for chemical activity.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. At the level of republics or armies, who was the one who could reach a decision that such chemical agents can be used for temporary disabling those who are causing problems?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR KESEROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Only officers at the level of the army command and higher.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] P1297, please. Can we please have that on the screen. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: As we can see, these are the rules of military police.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Page 3, please. There we'll be able to see what this is. 3 in e-court. Thank you. We can see here this is the rules of service for the military police of the armed forces of the SFRY. In the English version it will be on the following page. Can we now please see page 16, item 36. Or maybe let's just find item 36 in both versions. In English, it's on page 18, there we will find item 36. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. We see it on the screen now, and I'll read from item 36 of the rules of the SFRY armed forces military police: "The military police may use other means of coercion, (chemical means for temporary incapacitation, special vehicles, devices for forcibly halting vehicles) only in extraordinary cases, upon an authorisation by a commander of the army and other high-ranking military officer." That was your answer, wasn't it? Could you please now tell us whether these means for temporary incapacitation, can they leave permanent traces or permanently leave a mark on a person against whom they were used?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR KESEROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: If someone was only once exposed to it, no, that's why it's described as temporary incapacitation. In most cases, it would not leave any serious consequences.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. Up until 1995 in former JNA, could they also be used in the VRS in accordance to international laws and conventions?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR KESEROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, all these means were on the lists of means that were allowed, and, as far as I know, any police in the world or army in the world is still using them.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you, General. Can we now please see page 6 on our screens, since we have the rules in front of us because that will give us an opportunity to clear up something about the difference between a military commander and the commander of the military police. First of all, on that page we can see the introduction, and in the third paragraph of the introduction, we can read the following: "The regulations are intended for the following: Members of the armed police for their unified approach when executing their tasks from their jurisdiction, officers in commands, staffs, units of institutions of the armed forces within which the military police are organised for their unified command and control." And my question is: This unified command at all levels in all units of the military police on the territory of the state where the rules are applied, can you explain that for us?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR KESEROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That means that it is set up in such a way that within all units officers of certain level have equal rights of commanding units that are part of their complement in the same way, and to use them.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you, General. Does that mean that commanding over a soldier in Banja Luka and a soldier in Belgrade must be the same and that the officer in Banja Luka and officer in Belgrade also has to act in accordance with the rules of service for military police?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR KESEROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, of course, regardless of where he is located.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. My next question, because of this unified behaviour or action to achieve that, are officers and soldiers sent for training where they learn how they can arrest someone, and so on, how they will be carrying out all their tasks, to be more precise?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR KESEROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The training programme for military police was different to training programmes of other infantry units and it involved, inter alia, the training that was additional to what was provided for by the general rules of service in JNA and later VRS. It was complemented by the rules for the military police, and if I'm not mistaken, there were 14 such elements in the rules specific for the military police.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we now move to page 9 in e-court where we see the discussion about command and control or directing over military police.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Tolimir, before you start with the next line of questions, I think it's a convenient time to have our second break for today. Do you agree? Thank you. We must have our second break and resume quarter past 6.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Tolimir, as usual, you have provided us with an update of the list of documents to be used with the witness. I just note for the record that you have not included four documents you have used so far. This is D329, D193, P1011 and P1430. We would appreciate if you could include all documents you want to use for the benefit of the Chamber and the other party. Now you may continue your examination. Mr. Tolimir.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President. I apologise if those documents are not in e-court. I will make sure that they be uploaded and had I known that they weren't there, I wouldn't have used them. Before us is --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: It's a misunderstanding. I'm not talking about e-court. They are all in e-court. This is not the problem. But they are not in the list you have provided us with, the list of documents to be used. This is for the benefit, especially for the Prosecution that they know in advance which document you want to use. Please carry on.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President. I will make sure that something like that does not happen again. It is not customary either for myself or Mr. Gajic to do things like that.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Mr. Keserovic, before us we see the command and control of the military police rule. I will just put questions to you because I believe you are the most meritorious person to give answers in relation to this topic. I will not lead you in any way because you are the expert on this. In item 12, we see how military police is it to be commanded and controlled. Could you please tell us who is the only person who is authorised to command and control military police units at all levels of command?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR KESEROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The commander of the unit within which this military police unit is located.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. Is there any other officer who can command and control the military police, except the commander who is their superior officer?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR KESEROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not within the command hierarchy. There is only the matter of professional control.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Within the sphere of professional control, is it true that only the security organs that have been properly trained can do that, people who are familiar with how military police has to be used?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR KESEROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The commander of the organ of security is the one who controls in that respect, in professional respect, the military police. But there is another element which involves organs of traffic service, where in the sphere of security of military traffic, they are entitled to provide professional control to the unit that is in charge of traffic.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Is the traffic military police department also subordinated to the commander of the unit?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR KESEROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. All specialties, all units of military police, whatever their purpose is, are subordinated to the commander of the unit where they are.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. Would you please read second paragraph of item 13 before you and then tell us whether the same rights and duties are in possession of the officer who is in charge of the military police in relation to an officer who is in charge of arms and services?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR KESEROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. It is the same situation.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. Is it so because of the fact that the law provides only for a relationship between military police/security organs and the relevant commanding officer?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR KESEROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, these rules are based on the laws. You first have the laws that regulate the matter and then based on that one drafts the rules.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Would you please be so kind and show us page 8 in the e-court, item number 7. Thank you. Here we see item number 7 in the Serbian version. Can we please get it in the English version which is on the following page. Yes, here we see it.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Can you please explain to everyone present why it is prohibited to use military police for other activities that are outside of their scope of their normal activities? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR KESEROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The units of military police are not to be used outside of their needs and tasks for different activities, regardless of the type of activities, duty services, various works carried out by units, and so and on so forth, because these units are specialised units with special authorities that are regulated by the laws and the rules of service and because of the role they have within the system of defence within the armed forces, they should not be used for non-standard tasks. That would be the definition, in brief.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we now move to page 9 in e-court, item 12 in both versions, please. Page 9 in e-court, item 12.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: My question is the following: Military police unit of a brigade, can it be under the command of a senior officer of the military police from another brigade?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR KESEROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Can you explain why?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR KESEROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You can't have units of military police of one brigade under command of any officer who wasn't put to a position of a commander by some order. It is possible that sometimes more units of military police work together and that after re-subordination -- but the only officer that can command the military police unit is the commanding officer of that police unit.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you, General. Can we please -- or can you please read the second paragraph in item 13 where senior officers of the security organs are discussed and then tell us why is it that the senior officer of the security organ in relation to military police is placed in the same position as the chief of branches in relation to different branch --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's correction: Of arms, combat arms within the military.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In the military, in the armed forces that we are familiar with and that existed in the area in the armed forces and in the units, the basic principles of unity of command and subordination are applied so that means that only one commander can exist in a unit and he is responsible for everything. Functional or professional relationship exists in all combat arms and services, but it is restricted only to the rights and duties of professional management and control of those combat arms and services, or rather, the units of those combat arms and services. The law does not separate them. The rules also do not separate them. We have already spoken about that. In other words, they are equal. The security organ's relationship to the military police is the same as the head of musical department to the military orchestra.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I was going to correct the interpretation but it seems to be okay, my legal advisor tells me. Can we now look at page 13 in e-court, item 25(b). Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. We can see it now. I'm going to quote bullet point (b) where it says 25(b): "Take part in preventing the activities by any armed enemy groups or individuals who have been infiltrated or left behind on the axes of movement in the areas to which commands, institutions, and staffs of the armed forces have been deployed, and in temporarily occupied territory." My question is this: Is it in keeping with this bullet point 25(b) that the commander had the right to send the then Lieutenant-Colonel Savcic to prevent activities by infiltrated groups at the command post? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR KESEROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: If that refers to the battalion of the military police from the protection regiment, protection motorised regiment, and the entire protection motorised regiment had the same task, that task was rightly assigned.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. Bearing that in mind, bearing in mind what you've just told us, was the commander in a position to assign any individual in the command to participate in the prevention of attacks and diversions that were undertaken by the sabotage groups against the Main Staff? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR KESEROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Fight against sabotage and terrorist infiltrated groups or groups left behind is an obligation and a right equally applied to all units, commands, staffs, and institutions irrespective of the time and place when such fight is necessary. This specially applies to terrorist and sabotage group and fight against them is the universal right of all army members.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. Let's wait for the interpretation to stop. When it comes to the use of the military police in combat against infiltrated terrorist groups, such as were the terrorist groups from Srebrenica and Zepa that infiltrated to launch an attack against the Main Staff, would the same rule apply to a fight against sabotage groups? Would that be one of the regular tasks of the military police?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR KESEROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I am afraid that I did not understand your question. However, I believe that that was a regular task of every military police unit. Every police military unit has a detachment for anti-sabotage and anti-terrorist fight. People who are specially educated for that fight.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. Can you tell us when you contacted Malinic, did you learn if an anti-terrorist company had been sent to assist the Main Staff? Was it used in that way by the commander of the protection regiment and the commander of the Main Staff? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR KESEROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe that I have already testified about that, and I said that an anti-terrorist company and some other forces were in the sector of the Main Staff at the time and that they were fighting the groups that had been infiltrated and engaged in combat. Some were engaged in the Trnovo front line in the Sarajevo theatre of war, and in the Kasaba sector only a company of young soldiers in training remained.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. We were shown a document in this courtroom, or rather, could you please be shown D64, first of all. And then we will talk about very specific actions by the security organs of the military police once we have looked at the document. Thank you. We can see it now on the screen. This document was issued on the 12th of July to the intelligence and security departments and to the command of the Sarajevo-Romanija Corps and the Eastern Bosnian corps. If you look at the document, we will see that it says, amongst other things, in its fourth paragraph, "Those who communicated over the radio network," actually, this is the third paragraph. You can also say that it is the fourth paragraph, in any case: "Those who communicated over the radio network were probably in the Zvornik-Sehovic road and in the sector of Cerska. According to the number of communicators, it seemed to be divided into several groups headed by Ibrahim Mandzic, aka Mandza, one of Naser Oric's deputies." A new radio network was discovered on the 12th of July and its participants are mentioned in the document further on. It says in the sixth paragraph --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. McCloskey.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Your Honour, if -- he is going so fast you can tell the interpreter didn't get half of that paragraph because he was going so fast, and she would normally try to read it from the original translation, if they can get some help from there. But when everyone goes so fast they can't do that and this is an important document, so I would hope that we would slow down a bit. Obviously no hurry, we are going into next week.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Indeed. And there's another danger that sometimes the court reporter can't get which is part of your quotation and which is are your own words. Therefore, please slow down a bit. Carry on.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, I'll bear that in mind. I will repeat everything from the beginning.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: We see a strictly confidential document issued on the 12th of July and sent from the Main Staff, or, on behalf of the Main Staff, to the intelligence departments to the command of the Sarajevo-Romanija Corps and the Eastern Bosnia Corps. In the document it says, in the second paragraph, and I quote: "On 12 July of this year," and it was in 1995, "at 1945 hours, a radio network of elements of the 28th Muslim Division was activated; during the morning, at around 0500 hours, these elements came across our minefield in the sector of Ravni Buljim at the juncture between the Milic and Bratunac Brigades." "The individuals communicating over the radio network are probably in the sector of the Cerska and the Zvornik-Sekovici road. According to the number of communicators, they seem to be divided into several groups headed by Ibrahim Mandzic, aka, Mandza, one of Naser Oric's deputies." My question is this: Was this information received about elements of the 28th Division that had set out from Srebrenica and attempted a break-through on the access specified in this document? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR KESEROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This document indicates that those were indeed units of the 28th Division.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. If we look at the fifth paragraph from the bottom in the document, we will see that it says: "All electronic surveillance units of the Sarajevo-Romanija Corps, the Eastern Bosnia Corps and the Drina Corps, shall focus on surveillance and monitoring radio communications between these Muslim groups which operate on frequency 164 800." My question: Did the superior officer from the sector or from the security administration have the right to issue an order or to propose the engagement of the electronic surveillance unit to monitor that radio communication and that radio network? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR KESEROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not sure that I had a good look at the heading. I don't think that this is a document issued by the Main Staff. It was rather issued by the security department of the Drina Corps. But it doesn't really matter, the monitoring of certain frequencies is a purpose task by units for electronic surveillance and monitoring. So this --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Now you can see the headline of the document in B/C/S. Mr. McCloskey.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: It would be fair to let the witness see who the document is from. I mean, who is it authored by so he can -- as he is speaking as an expert on this document, given where he was on the 12th of July, but if he is going to be asked about it, he should be able to see who authored it which he hasn't seen yet.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Can the electronic courtroom move the document to display the stamp for the benefit of the witness so that the witness may see who signed the document and which command issued a document. And then at the top you also see the recipients, the command who received the document.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Now that you see that, now that you see the signature of Zdravko Tolimir, are you able to determine?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR KESEROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Now that I see both the top part as well as the bottom part or the beginning thereof, this is obviously a forwarded document that was first issued by the Main Staff and sent to the corps, and then the corps forwarded it to the electronic surveillance and monitoring unit. If the signature of General Tolimir was lost in the process, that would mean that it was done without an authority, or rather, that one commander of the corps issues an order to another commander of the corps. But since it was sent by the chief of the sector from the Main Staff, this would be in compliance with the valid rules.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. Please look at the following paragraph.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: I would like to see the heading of the document in both versions. It says here in the English version, "Command of the Drina Corps Intelligence Department." Do you see that, sir? I'm asking the witness.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, yes, I can see that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. McCloskey.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Yes, and General Tolimir, and again it may be a translation issue, but said as you can see the signature at the bottom from General Tolimir. Of course, we can't see that and there is no signature on this document. It's a teletype document. So I just wanted to clarify that for the record because that was just incorrect.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: That happens quite frequently. We should go to the next page again in both languages. Indeed, we see here the name Nacelnik General-Major Zdravko Tolimir without a specific handwritten signature. Mr. Tolimir, please carry on.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: General, you can see that the telegram went under the name of Major-General Zdravko Tolimir?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR KESEROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can see that.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Does that indicate that the document was issued at the level of the Main Staff?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR KESEROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Please, let's look at page 1 again, third paragraph from the bottom, beginning with the word "organs": "Intelligence and security organs of the brigade commands shall propose to the commanders of units positioned along the line of withdrawal of elements of the routed 28th Muslim Division from Srebrenica to undertake all measures to prevent the withdrawal of enemy soldiers and to capture them." Is this a proposal or an order?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR KESEROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is a proposal, or rather, this is a task given to security organs to propose to their own commanders a mode of engagement in fighting the 28th Division, that they should propose it.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we scroll down to see the last two lines. Next page in English.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: I quote: "The Muslims want to portray Srebrenica as having been demilitarised and populated only by civilians. And that is why they ordered all armed men fit for military service to pull out from the area illegally, across the territory of Republika Srpska, to Muslim controlled territory, so that they could accuse the VRS of an unprovoked attack on civilians in a protected area. "Although it is very important to arrest as many members of the crushed Muslim units as possible, or liquidate them if they resist, it is equally important to note down the names of all men fit for military service who are being evacuated from the UNPROFOR base in Potocari." Now, Mr. Keserovic, in the paragraph that I quoted, is it emphasised why it is necessary to list everyone and to capture as many of these groups and to list all those leaving Potocari? Can we see why this was proposed -- to be proposed to the commanders?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR KESEROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: From the context of this document to the extent I was able to read it, this registration of those who are being evacuated and capturing others was necessary in order to counter the Muslim attempt to portray the zone as demilitarised while the Republika Srpska authorities knew very well it was not. By listing all those who were armed and fit for military service, it would have been possible to do that. I believe that was the purpose, just based on the context.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Based on the context of this document, can we infer that the person who is suggesting to security organs to propose to their own commanders to take this action, can we infer what the author wanted to achieve with this registration?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR KESEROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think we can infer that.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. Is this proposal to register some and capture others legitimate both from the point of view of military activities and security related activities in terms of what was being sought, in terms of the intention?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR KESEROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: At any rate, it was in keeping with the current rules of combat, rules of engagement.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Mr. Keserovic, tell us, did security organs act in accordance with this rule, and did you know about that from your contacts with the military police and security and intelligence organs?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR KESEROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, my hands-on experience from the war shows that security organs mainly complied with the rules.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: In the course of examination-in-chief, you said that Major Malinic, commander of the military police battalion, told you that he listed and registered the prisoners of war he had up until a point when Mladic showed up to address them. Do you remember that or shall I show you a transcript?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR KESEROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I remember that. I said it more than one.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: In that particular case, did Major Malinic act in accordance with the instructions of the superior security organs, in this case the staff of the battalion?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR KESEROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He was perfectly within the rules when he was listing those people. If I'm remembering this well, he had received instructions given originally by Colonel Beara, and he proceeded to list the prisoners. That was in keeping with the rules.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Keserovic. Since we have only one minute left, I want to wish you a pleasant weekend and to apologise that I didn't ask before if it causes you great inconvenience to stay until Monday. But I wanted to take advantage of this time and ask all the questions I needed to.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, this is all I had for today. If there's nothing else -- if the witness has to go, we can live with that and we can perhaps arrange to recall him at a later stage.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Before I come to that question, I have only one question for the witness at the moment: Who was the commander of the Drina Corps at this relevant time in the middle of July 1995?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, in the early days of the Krivaja operation, the corps commander was General Zivanovic. A day or two after the entry into Srebrenica, General Krstic was appointed corps commander so that both were commanders of the corps at different stages of the operation. I'm not sure on which day the hand-over of -- the transition of duty took place. In some documents General Zivanovic is the signatory, but as of 13 July, General Krstic is signed as commander in some documents.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Thank you very much. We have to adjourn for the week. We will resume on Monday, 2.15 and Mr. Tolimir will continue his cross-examination and finish it at that time, and Mr. McCloskey will then commence his re-examination. On Monday, 2.15 in Courtroom III. Thank you very much. We adjourn.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Monday, the 16th day of May, 2011, at 2.15 p.m.

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 7.01 p.m.
